### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.pick

### Question

Hi,
First of all, thank you so much echasnovski for `mini.nvim`. My config's been based off it nearly since I started with Neovim about a year ago.

Is it possible to disable hlsearch in the `mini.pick` floating window? I find it annoying when I search for something and then the matches show up as I'm using fuzzy picking something else entirely.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2c162b5-c969-4e8c-b8a5-5d84fbe284c2

I've tried the these autocommands, but they don't work.
```lua
_G.Config = {}
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
  pattern = 'MiniPickStart',
  callback = function()
    Config.hlsearch = vim.v.hlsearch
    vim.v.hlsearch = 0
  end,
})
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
  pattern = 'MiniPickStop',
  callback = function()
    vim.v.hlsearch = Config.hlsearch
  end,
})
```
Using `vim.v.hlsearch` never works. Setting `vim.o.hlsearch = false` on `MiniPickStart` does work, but then search highlights can only _always_ or never be shown after closing `mini.pick`, not restored to the previous state.

Does anyone known how to achieve this?

comment_data.body:
Hi! Thanks for kind words!

> I've tried the these autocommands, but they don't work.

This is the right direction and is very close to the solution. Handling of highlight search state is indeed not the smoothest it can be in Neovim (or in Vim, rather).

The final piece of the puzzle is to handle the `hlsearch` variable not directly inside an autocommand callback, but a bit later. For that, wrap each callback in `vim.schedule_wrap`. This note from `:h :nohlsearch` (pointing to `:h autocmd-searchpat` for more details) can probably explain why:

> This command doesn't work in an autocommand, because the highlighting state is saved and restored when executing autocommands |autocmd-searchpat|. Same thing for when invoking a user function.

Here is the version of autocommands that seem to work:

```lua
local hlsearch_old = vim.v.hlsearch

local disable_hl = vim.schedule_wrap(function()
  hlsearch_old = vim.v.hlsearch
  vim.v.hlsearch = 0
end)
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStart', callback = disable_hl })

local restore_hl = vim.schedule_wrap(function() vim.v.hlsearch = hlsearch_old end)
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStop', callback = restore_hl })
```

---

To add to this, I don't think the "temporarily disable hlsearch" is a universally good idea. For me it is occasionally intentionally useful to see matches of what I previously searched for inside preview and/or items.

An alternative solution can be a custom mapping for `:nohlsearch`. Something like this:

```lua
require('mini.pick').setup({
  mappings = {
    nohlsearch = { char = '<C-h>', func = function() vim.cmd('nohlsearch') end },
    scroll_left = '',
  },
})
```
